# Protobuf API reference

Messages, fields, enums, and services shared by Luxir's HTTP and gRPC APIs.
See the [gRPC guide](../guide/grpc.md) for client generation and streaming,
and [HTTP JSON mappings](../guide/grpc.md#http-json-versus-protobuf-values)
for the HTTP shorthands.

Field descriptions come from the protobuf source comments. `optional` marks
explicit field presence; `oneof` members share a single choice. Application
defaults and constraints are described in the comments and guides.

<a id="message-luxir.analyzercomponent"></a>

### luxir.AnalyzerComponent

One analysis-chain component - a tokenizer or a token filter - named by its registry name, plus its parameters. params values are typed JSON values (string, number, bool, string list), e.g. {"possessive": false} for kstem. A component that takes no parameters rejects any. The JSON dialect accepts a bare string for a parameterless component: "lowercase" == {"name": "lowercase"}.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.analyzercomponent.name"></a>[`name`](#field-luxir.analyzercomponent.name) | 1 | `string` | singular | e.g., "unicode\_word", "nfkc\_cf" |
| <a id="field-luxir.analyzercomponent.params"></a>[`params`](#field-luxir.analyzercomponent.params) | 2 | map&lt;`string`, [`Val`](#message-luxir.val)&gt; | map |  |

<a id="message-luxir.anyofquery"></a>

### luxir.AnyOfQuery

Constant-score exact value-set membership using the field's value binding. TEXT values are analyzed: zero tokens contribute nothing, one token is accepted, and multiple tokens are an error. STRING values use the field's normalizer; ID values remain verbatim before applying long\_terms. Numeric and DATE values use the same scalar coercion as ingest.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.anyofquery.field"></a>[`field`](#field-luxir.anyofquery.field) | 1 | `string` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.anyofquery.values"></a>[`values`](#field-luxir.anyofquery.values) | 2 | [`Val`](#message-luxir.val) | singular | Required scalar or array of scalars. Null and nested arrays are errors. An empty array matches nothing; duplicate values are ignored. |

<a id="message-luxir.cachecontrolrequest"></a>

### luxir.CacheControlRequest

Admin control over the per-collection query cache. Actions compose and apply in this order: flush, reset\_admission, reset\_counters, then dump. flush drops resident values and entry metadata; sighting history survives, so a known query can be readmitted and rebuilt immediately. flush + reset\_admission also forgets sightings, restarting admission tracking. reset\_counters zeroes the cumulative stats. An empty collection targets every collection.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.collection"></a>[`collection`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.collection) | 1 | `string` | singular | empty selects every collection |
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.flush"></a>[`flush`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.flush) | 2 | `bool` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.reset_admission"></a>[`reset_admission`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.reset_admission) | 3 | `bool` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.reset_counters"></a>[`reset_counters`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.reset_counters) | 4 | `bool` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.dump"></a>[`dump`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.dump) | 5 | `bool` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.dump_limit"></a>[`dump_limit`](#field-luxir.cachecontrolrequest.dump_limit) | 6 | `uint32` | singular | max dump rows per shard; 0 = 100 |

<a id="message-luxir.cacheentrydump"></a>

### luxir.CacheEntryDump

One resident cache entry. key\_text is the printable-byte extraction from the serialized key (field names and terms survive; structure bytes do not); key\_hash is a diagnostic fingerprint. bytes counts resident value payloads; segments\_resident counts slots currently holding a value; reader\_value marks a whole-reader live-exact value.

<a id="message-luxir.commitparams"></a>

### luxir.CommitParams

Parameters governing how a commit is performed. Presence of this message in an UpdateRequest indicates the request should commit; absence means no commit.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.commitparams.commit_within_ms"></a>[`commit_within_ms`](#field-luxir.commitparams.commit_within_ms) | 1 | `uint64` | singular | Commit deadline in milliseconds. 0 (default) commits before responding; a positive value schedules a deferred commit and responds without waiting. Deferred requests coalesce at the earliest outstanding deadline. An explicit commit also satisfies outstanding deadlines. max\_segments, build\_aux\_indexes, or wait\_for\_merges force an immediate commit instead. Search visibility also depends on SearchRequest.freshness\_ms. |
| <a id="field-luxir.commitparams.build_aux_indexes"></a>[`build_aux_indexes`](#field-luxir.commitparams.build_aux_indexes) | 2 | `string` | repeated | Build missing aux overlays as part of this commit. An overlay already present on a segment is retained rather than rebuilt. \[\] - request no aux builds \["\*"\] - build every eligible missing vector overlay \["vec.title\_v"\] - build the missing vector overlay for title\_v Only "\*" and exact overlay names are supported; no partial-name patterns. |
| <a id="field-luxir.commitparams.wait_for_merges"></a>[`wait_for_merges`](#field-luxir.commitparams.wait_for_merges) | 3 | `bool` | singular | If true, this commit will wait for any in-flight merges to finish before publishing. |
| <a id="field-luxir.commitparams.max_segments"></a>[`max_segments`](#field-luxir.commitparams.max_segments) | 4 | `uint32` | singular | Merge down so the data visible at this commit resides in at most this many segments. 0 (default) = no forced merging. The response is not sent until the merged index is durably published: at return, everything this commit made visible lives in &lt;= max\_segments segments (concurrent ingestion after this commit may add new segments; they are not covered by the promise). The response waits for the merged layout even when commit\_within\_ms is positive. |

<a id="message-luxir.error"></a>

### luxir.Error

A failure. The same shape everywhere an error appears: SearchResponse.error, UpdateResponse.error and its per-document errors, the HTTP error body, and gRPC status details. kind is the coarse class: it selects the HTTP status and gRPC status code, and tells a client whether to fix the request, the target, or retry, without knowing the code. code is the stable machine key (snake\_case, like Warning.code); new codes appear under existing kinds without changing this shape. message is human detail, not a contract.

<a id="message-luxir.exprquery"></a>

### luxir.ExprQuery

An expression in the Luxir query language, with strict syntax and precise parse errors. Raw search-box input can use SimpleQuery. Expressions have structured Query equivalents and use the same field analysis rules.<br><br>Syntax summary: field:value, field:"a phrase" (or '...'), field:(grouped boolean scope), AND / OR / NOT with real precedence (NOT &gt; AND &gt; OR), +required / -prohibited prefixes (may not mix with AND/OR at one level), ranges field:\[a TO b\] / {a TO b} and comparisons field:&gt;=v, trailing \* for prefix, term~N for fuzzy (bare ~ = auto), \*:\* matches everything, and the function form name(main value, arg=value, ...) reaching the callable query types by their JSON names (kNN and geo queries require structured messages). $name references a value bound in \`vars\`. Unfielded bare words are a parse error.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.exprquery.q"></a>[`q`](#field-luxir.exprquery.q) | 1 | `string` | singular | the expression |
| <a id="field-luxir.exprquery.vars"></a>[`vars`](#field-luxir.exprquery.vars) | 2 | map&lt;`string`, [`Val`](#message-luxir.val)&gt; | map | Values referenced from the expression as $name. Bound as VALUES (never re-parsed as syntax), so end-user input is safe to pass through: {"q": "simple\_query($input, fields=\[title\])", "vars": {"input": ...}}. |

<a id="message-luxir.fielddefaults"></a>

### luxir.FieldDefaults

Default representations for bare field names. Each binding names "self" or a local variant label. Absent inherits the parent's defaults; present replaces both bindings. An omitted value binding on a TEXT primary selects its sole STRING variant; an omitted search binding on a STRING primary selects its sole TEXT variant. Multiple candidates require an explicit binding. With no candidate, or for other type combinations, use self. Inference uses resolved types; operations still check index/column support. Explicit &lt;field&gt;\_\_&lt;label&gt; and &lt;field&gt;\_\_self selectors bypass these defaults.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.fielddefaults.search"></a>[`search`](#field-luxir.fielddefaults.search) | 1 | `string` | optional | Match, phrase, simple query, expression terms, prefix, fuzzy, wildcard, and regex queries, including their use in filters. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fielddefaults.value"></a>[`value`](#field-luxir.fielddefaults.value) | 2 | `string` | optional | AnyOfQuery, ranges, field/range facets, sorts, and column expressions. Bare field names in retrieval, exists, kNN, and geo use the primary. |

<a id="message-luxir.fusion"></a>

### luxir.Fusion

Hybrid-search fusion: run several source queries (each a full TopDocs spec) and merge their results into a single ranked list.<br><br>Per-source response-shape fields (\`fields\`, \`batch\_size\`, \`offset\`, \`get\_scores\`, \`get\_number\`, \`document\_format\`) are ignored - Fusion controls response shape at the top level. Per-source \`ops\` are rejected; put facets and metrics in Fusion.ops. Each source's \`query\`, \`sort\`, \`limit\`, and any per-source \`filter\` are used to produce that source's ranked list.<br><br>The fusion-level \`filter\` is ANDed with each source's own filters.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

<a id="oneof-luxir.fusion.method"></a>

**oneof `method`:** at most one member can be set.

Required fusion method.

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.sources"></a>[`sources`](#field-luxir.fusion.sources) | 1 | map&lt;`string`, [`TopDocs`](#message-luxir.topdocs)&gt; | map | Named source queries. At least one source is required. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.filter"></a>[`filter`](#field-luxir.fusion.filter) | 2 | [`Filter`](#message-luxir.filter) | repeated | Filters applied to every source. except\_ops is not supported here or in source filters. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.limit"></a>[`limit`](#field-luxir.fusion.limit) | 3 | `sint64` | optional | Maximum fused documents to return. Unset = 10; 0 = none; -1 = all remaining. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.rrf"></a>[`rrf`](#field-luxir.fusion.rrf) | 10 | [`RrfFusion`](#message-luxir.rrffusion) | oneof [`method`](#oneof-luxir.fusion.method) |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.offset"></a>[`offset`](#field-luxir.fusion.offset) | 4 | `int64` | singular | Response shape (mirrors TopDocs). Zero-based rank of the first returned fused document; must be &gt;= 0. Return up to limit after skipping. Source limits remain candidate-pool sizes: paging cannot reach beyond the union of their ranked windows. Each response DocList.offset is the absolute rank of that batch's first row, or the requested offset for an empty page. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.get_number"></a>[`get_number`](#field-luxir.fusion.get_number) | 5 | `bool` | singular | return the number of distinct documents in the source union |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.get_scores"></a>[`get_scores`](#field-luxir.fusion.get_scores) | 6 | `bool` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.fields"></a>[`fields`](#field-luxir.fusion.fields) | 7 | `string` | repeated | as TopDocs.fields: empty returns every retrievable field, '\*' patterns expand |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.batch_size"></a>[`batch_size`](#field-luxir.fusion.batch_size) | 8 | `int32` | singular | same batching rules as TopDocs.batch\_size |
| <a id="field-luxir.fusion.document_format"></a>[`document_format`](#field-luxir.fusion.document_format) | 9 | [`DocFormat`](#enum-luxir.docformat) | singular | rows vs columns placement of returned fields (see DocFormat) |

<a id="message-luxir.fuzzyquery"></a>

### luxir.FuzzyQuery

Matches indexed terms within byte-wise Levenshtein distance of \`term\`. TEXT fields apply multi-term normalization without tokenization; STRING fields apply their normalizer and ID fields use it verbatim. Scoring queries use blended BM25 statistics; filter queries use constant scores.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |

| <a id="field-luxir.fuzzyquery.field"></a>[`field`](#field-luxir.fuzzyquery.field) | 1 | `string` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.fuzzyquery.term"></a>[`term`](#field-luxir.fuzzyquery.term) | 2 | `string` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.fuzzyquery.max_edits"></a>[`max_edits`](#field-luxir.fuzzyquery.max_edits) | 3 | `int32` | optional | Maximum edit distance, 0..2. Unset = AUTO by term length: 0 for &lt;=2 bytes, 1 for &lt;=5, else 2. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fuzzyquery.prefix_length"></a>[`prefix_length`](#field-luxir.fuzzyquery.prefix_length) | 4 | `int32` | optional | Leading bytes that must match exactly. Unset = 1; 0 = no required prefix. |
| <a id="field-luxir.fuzzyquery.max_expansions"></a>[`max_expansions`](#field-luxir.fuzzyquery.max_expansions) | 5 | `int32` | singular | Max term expansions, closest terms first. Unset/0 = default 50. A positive value requests that cap; the operator/clause budget may lower it with a warning. Negative values are rejected. |

<a id="message-luxir.geoboxquery"></a>

### luxir.GeoBoxQuery

Inclusive geographic bounding box in degrees. Bounds are quantized to the storage grid exactly like ingest. min\_lon &gt; max\_lon crosses the dateline; min\_lat &gt; max\_lat is an error. Boxes degenerate at +90 latitude or +180 longitude match nothing.<br><br>Named scalar bounds deliberately avoid positional ambiguity: the VALUE array contract \[x, y\] = \[lon, lat\] does not apply to this message.

<a id="message-luxir.knnquery"></a>

### luxir.KnnQuery

Nearest-neighbor query against a searchable vector field. Search is exact when no ANN index is available; an ANN index may produce approximate results. The query vector must be non-empty and match the field's dimensions. Deleted documents and documents outside the enclosing domain are excluded. Multi-valued fields return one hit per document using its highest similarity.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.field"></a>[`field`](#field-luxir.knnquery.field) | 1 | `string` | singular | vector field name (e.g. "embedding\_v") |
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.query"></a>[`query`](#field-luxir.knnquery.query) | 2 | [`Vector`](#message-luxir.vector) | singular | query vector - must match the field's dims |
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.k"></a>[`k`](#field-luxir.knnquery.k) | 3 | `int32` | singular | number of nearest-neighbor documents to return; must be positive |
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.exact"></a>[`exact`](#field-luxir.knnquery.exact) | 4 | `bool` | singular | Require exact top-k results by scanning stored vectors. Cost is linear in the number of stored vectors; refine\_candidates and ivf are ignored. |
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.refine_candidates"></a>[`refine_candidates`](#field-luxir.knnquery.refine_candidates) | 5 | `int32` | singular | Candidate-pool size for full-precision rescoring of ANN results, before collapsing multiple vectors to one hit per document. Clamped up to k; 0 selects an adaptive default. Larger pools can improve recall at a cost in memory and latency. Fewer candidates may be available. |
| <a id="field-luxir.knnquery.ivf"></a>[`ivf`](#field-luxir.knnquery.ivf) | 6 | [`KnnQuery.Ivf`](#message-luxir.knnquery.ivf) | singular | ignored for exact search and segments without an IVF index |

<a id="message-luxir.rangequery"></a>

### luxir.RangeQuery

Matches documents whose field value falls in the given range. All bounds are optional; omit a side for an open-ended range. Set at most one of gte/gt (lower) and at most one of lte/lt (upper); setting both of a pair is an error. With no bounds the query matches every document that has a value for the field. A doc with no value never matches.<br><br>Numeric fields (INT/FLOAT/DOUBLE/DATE) require a column. Bounds go through the same value-coercion contract as ingest, so querying a literal finds the documents ingested with it. DATE accepts ISO-8601 strings or epoch millis, and a partial date names its whole window: bounds include the granule they name (\[2024-01 TO 2024-06\] covers January through June; exclusive bounds exclude the granule whole). FLOAT/DOUBLE compare by IEEE-754 total order: -0.0 sorts below +0.0 and NaN sorts above +Inf.<br><br>Term-backed fields (TEXT/STRING/ID) range over indexed terms in byte order (no collation), constant-scoring. TEXT bounds use multi-term normalization without tokenization; STRING bounds use the field's normalizer. Exact bounds follow the field's long\_terms policy. Uses the field's value binding.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.rangequery.field"></a>[`field`](#field-luxir.rangequery.field) | 1 | `string` | singular |  |
| <a id="field-luxir.rangequery.gte"></a>[`gte`](#field-luxir.rangequery.gte) | 2 | [`Val`](#message-luxir.val) | singular | lower bound, inclusive (&gt;=) |
| <a id="field-luxir.rangequery.gt"></a>[`gt`](#field-luxir.rangequery.gt) | 3 | [`Val`](#message-luxir.val) | singular | lower bound, exclusive (&gt;) |
| <a id="field-luxir.rangequery.lte"></a>[`lte`](#field-luxir.rangequery.lte) | 4 | [`Val`](#message-luxir.val) | singular | upper bound, inclusive (&lt;=) |
| <a id="field-luxir.rangequery.lt"></a>[`lt`](#field-luxir.rangequery.lt) | 5 | [`Val`](#message-luxir.val) | singular | upper bound, exclusive (&lt;) |

<a id="message-luxir.regexquery"></a>

### luxir.RegexQuery

Matches an anchored whole indexed term using \`\|\`, concatenation, groups, repetition, \`.\`, and character classes. \`^\` and \`$\` are literals. On TEXT fields, literal characters fold the way the field folds text; character classes and ranges are codepoint-exact. STRING fields also normalize literal characters; ID fields use literals verbatim.

<a id="message-luxir.segmentstats"></a>

### luxir.SegmentStats

Ids and generations that appear in filenames are reported in their filesystem spelling so stats output correlates directly with directory listings and logs: "seg" is the segment's data-file prefix (e.g. "s0a"), while generations are the length-prefixed base36 sortable strings embedded in filenames (e.g. live\_gen "01" -&gt; file "s0a\_\_L01"). Sortable strings order the same as the numbers they encode, so lexicographic comparison remains valid. Empty (omitted in JSON) means none. Generations that never appear on disk (index\_gen, core\_gen, update\_version) stay numeric.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |

<a id="message-luxir.simplequery"></a>

### luxir.SimpleQuery

Forgiving end-user query for raw search-box input. Malformed query text degrades to a valid query. Reported degradations appear in SearchResponse.warnings.<br><br>Syntax: bare words (searched across \`fields\`), + (the NEXT clause is required; needs a preceding clause to combine with, so a leading + is inert), -word (must not; under the default OR this is its own all-except-word clause - restrictive negation needs operator AND), a \| b (or), "a phrase", (grouping), trailing \* (prefix), word~N (fuzzy; bare ~ = auto edits), \\ escapes the next character, and field:value / field:"a phrase" fielded terms. A colon token whose field name is not queryable degrades to literal text against \`fields\`.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Field | Number | Type | Cardinality / group | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| <a id="field-luxir.simplequery.q"></a>[`q`](#field-luxir.simplequery.q) | 1 | `string` | singular | the raw user input |
| <a id="field-luxir.simplequery.fields"></a>[`fields`](#field-luxir.simplequery.fields) | 2 | `string` | repeated | The fields unfielded (bare) terms search; scores sum across fields. Required and non-empty. Invalid request parameters can cause errors even though malformed q text is tolerated. |
| <a id="field-luxir.simplequery.operator"></a>[`operator`](#field-luxir.simplequery.operator) | 3 | [`Match.Operator`](#enum-luxir.match.operator) | singular | How adjacent clauses combine. Unset = OR (any clause may match). |
| <a id="field-luxir.simplequery.min_match"></a>[`min_match`](#field-luxir.simplequery.min_match) | 4 | `int32` | singular | Minimum number of top-level optional clauses that must match (mirrors BooleanQuery.min\_match). Silently inapplicable when the parsed top level cannot honor it (a single clause, required clauses from + or the AND operator). |
| <a id="field-luxir.simplequery.allowed_fields"></a>[`allowed_fields`](#field-luxir.simplequery.allowed_fields) | 5 | `string` | repeated | Narrows which field names the field:value syntax may reach. Empty = every queryable schema field. It can only narrow that set - listing a name the schema cannot query does not make it work. A field: token outside the allowed set is literal text, never an error. |

Processing stops at the first failing document: documents already indexed by this request are rolled back, queued delete\_ids from this request are rolled back, and later documents are not attempted (and not listed in errors). Atomicity is per-request; it does not span multiple requests in a stream. |
| <a id="field-luxir.updaterequest.return_ids"></a>[`return_ids`](#field-luxir.updaterequest.return_ids) | 9 | `bool` | singular | If true, return the ids of indexed documents in the response. |

An entry mapping to "" drops that input key. After mapping, a name appearing more than once in a doc keeps the last occurrence (the same last-wins rule as duplicate keys). Keys not in the map index under their own name unless drop\_unmapped is set. This reshapes a foreign document stream per request, without editing the input or the schema. |
| <a id="field-luxir.updaterequest.drop_unmapped"></a>[`drop_unmapped`](#field-luxir.updaterequest.drop_unmapped) | 12 | `bool` | singular | If true, doc keys not present in field\_map are dropped instead of indexed. Requires a non-empty field\_map (note "id" is dropped too unless mapped). |

<a id="message-luxir.wildcardquery"></a>

### luxir.WildcardQuery

Matches an entire indexed term. \`\*\` matches any bytes, \`?\` matches one codepoint, and backslash escapes the next character. On TEXT fields, literal characters fold the way the field folds text; \`\*\`, \`?\`, and escapes are syntax and never fold. STRING fields also normalize literal characters; ID fields use literals verbatim.

<a id="enum-luxir.docformat"></a>

### luxir.DocFormat

Placement preference for returned document fields: dense columns (DocList.columns) vs per-document maps (DocList.docs). DEFAULT resolves per transport: HTTP/JSON -&gt; ROWS, gRPC -&gt; COLUMNS. Under COLUMNS, explicitly named fields are returned as dense columns while discovered fields (empty or wildcard selectors) use docs; under ROWS everything is returned in docs.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="value-luxir.docformat.default"></a>[`DEFAULT`](#value-luxir.docformat.default) | 0 |  |
| <a id="value-luxir.docformat.rows"></a>[`ROWS`](#value-luxir.docformat.rows) | 1 |  |
| <a id="value-luxir.docformat.columns"></a>[`COLUMNS`](#value-luxir.docformat.columns) | 2 |  |

<a id="enum-luxir.fielddef.indexmode"></a>

### luxir.FieldDef.IndexMode

Index acceleration. Numeric Match/Range and geographic predicates can scan a column with NONE. Term queries on STRING/TEXT/ID require MATCH; STRING columns alone do not provide term-query support.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.none"></a>[`NONE`](#value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.none) | 0 | no index |
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.match"></a>[`MATCH`](#value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.match) | 1 | term index for STRING/TEXT/ID, including term ranges |
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.range"></a>[`RANGE`](#value-luxir.fielddef.indexmode.range) | 2 | numeric Match/Range or GEO\_POINT predicates; requires column=true |

<a id="enum-luxir.fielddef.longterms"></a>

### luxir.FieldDef.LongTerms

Policy for indexed terms longer than 255 bytes: STRING after normalization, TEXT after analysis, and IDs. Exact query values use the same policy. Not valid on column-only STRING or other types. Changes do not rewrite existing terms. See docs/guide/schema.md for ordering and query implications.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.truncate"></a>[`TRUNCATE`](#value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.truncate) | 0 | keep a UTF-8-safe prefix of at most 255 bytes; values may merge |
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.reject"></a>[`REJECT`](#value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.reject) | 1 | reject overlong terms |
| <a id="value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.hash128"></a>[`HASH128`](#value-luxir.fielddef.longterms.hash128) | 2 | prefix of at most 230 bytes plus 25 base36 hash digits |

<a id="enum-luxir.selectionmode"></a>

### luxir.SelectionMode

How facet selections filter the enclosing TopDocs results and its sub-operations. Nonempty selected is supported only on facets directly in TopDocs.ops. Selections on different facets combine with AND. Domain overrides can discard these filters; see Domain.apply\_parent\_filters.

[Source](../../protos/luxir_types.proto)

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="value-luxir.selectionmode.any"></a>[`ANY`](#value-luxir.selectionmode.any) | 0 | match any selected value; omit this selection's filter from its own facet |
| <a id="value-luxir.selectionmode.all"></a>[`ALL`](#value-luxir.selectionmode.all) | 1 | Require every selected value. Keep this selection's filter on its own facet so each unselected bucket counts matches if that value is added. |
